messages:
omar: Heads-up — ran into a recurring micro-window tail this morning. small P95 jumps while aggregate throughput and GPU utilization look steady.
rachel: Saw the same. suspect the coalescer is folding large joiners into active windows and evicting recently-won tiny tickets.
linh: Paste a trace if you have one
omar: ```
# trace excerpt
0.000: enqueue tenant=fast, size=48
0.004: enqueue tenant=bulk, size=1500
0.008: coalesce window 8ms -> merged batch size 1548 -> slot owner upgraded to bulk
0.009: evict queued fast request held in slotX -> delayed 160ms
metrics: fast_p95=220ms, fast_p50=12ms
```
rachel: Idea: early-reserve policy for sub-64B requests. When a tiny request wins a slot, tag that slot with a short-lived protection token (early-reserve) that prevents eviction by bulk joiners for M windows unless global fill < threshold.
tomas: That's basically a slot-protection flag. Alternative is admission demux (fast lane vs bulk lane) so queues don't fight, but that increases queue surface and can hurt fill on small clusters.
linh: Two concerns: 1) fairness, attackers could send many tiny requests to hold protections; 2) state churn across handoffs — tags need to be cheap and not require global locks.
david: For fairness, couple slot protection with a per-tenant protection budget that decays and caps. If tenant exhausts budget, their tiny tickets lose protection until budget replenishes. Budget decay can be time-based or token-leak.
rachel: Implementation sketch: per-slot: uint8 flags {prot_bit, age_bucket}; per-tenant: uint16 protection_credits. On enqueue of tiny request: if credits>0 -> set prot_bit, decrement credits atomically. On eviction attempt: if prot_bit && global_fill>fill_target -> refuse eviction and mark reason=protected. Age_bucket increments each coalesce epoch and clears after N epochs.
linh: That keeps metadata minimal. Need to be careful with atomic ops on hot paths. Use CAS on slot flags and relaxed reads for eviction. Worst-case we conservatively block eviction when CAS races occur.
tomas: Observability: emit evict_decision={packed, shortage, protected}, metric protected_block_rate, tenant_protection_utilization, and small_tail_by_tenant. We should be able to slice by shard and model.
david: Cost modelling: bench mixed workload (70% tiny / 30% bulk), measure token-utilization and cost-per-token. Expect some utilization loss when protections are active; quantify break-even for latency-sensitive SLAs.
omar: Quick dev bench I ran: tiny_p95 dropped from 210ms->28ms; token-throughput -2.1%; estimated unit-cost +2.9%. Looks promising for latency-critical tiers.
linh: Edge case: KV-cache locality. If protection prevents merging, we might suffer cache misses for the bulk batch that would have benefited. Need KV-cache locality heuristic: if incoming bulk shares >K keys with batch, allow merge despite protection.
rachel: Good call. Add a merge override: if coalesce candidate overlap_score>key_overlap_threshold -> allow despite protection.
tomas: Rollout plan: feature-flag gate. Stages: bench harness -> perf-canary on low-traffic shards -> 1% prod -> 10% -> full. Gates: small_p95, overall unit-cost delta, protected_block_rate.
david: Also add automatic rollback if unit-cost delta > 6% or small_p95 doesn't improve after 1% stage.
infra-bot: CI started for branch rachel/slot-protect-proto (build 4991) :building_construction:
omar: I'll help write the RFC section on decision tradeoffs (demux vs tag), and add a short appendix with cost modeling equations. Ping when draft is up.
